key_insight: AgentSSL explores whether automated machine learning engineering (MLE) agents can use abundant unlabeled data when labeled examples are scarce. It frames semi-supervised learning as a search over programs, extending agent-driven pipeline design beyond fully supervised settings.
problem_solved: Adapting ML to new domains requires costly data labeling and manual pipeline engineering. Existing MLE agents have largely been studied in fully supervised settings, leaving their ability to exploit unlabeled data insufficiently evaluated.
method: Introduce Agentic Semi-Supervised Learning (AgentSSL) for settings with limited labeled data and abundant unlabeled data.
Frame semi-supervised learning pipeline development as a program search problem.
Study whether MLE agents can leverage unlabeled data; the provided abstract is truncated and does not specify the full evaluation or results.
impact: This work could help practitioners automate ML development in data-scarce domains while making use of unlabeled datasets. The supplied excerpt does not establish performance gains or labeling-cost reductions.
visual_elements: Data imbalance graphic: a small labeled dataset beside a large unlabeled dataset.
Workflow diagram: labeled and unlabeled data → MLE agent → program search → ML pipeline.
Side-by-side comparison of fully supervised and semi-supervised agent workflows.
Search-tree illustration showing candidate pipeline programs branching from an agent.
paper_title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
paper_authors: Ethan Lin, Akanksha Sarkar, Ziang Liu, Kristin Branson, Jennifer J. Sun
